notes: Burrow (Hydrogen/Shopify-Oxygen headless). Direct HTTP fetch throughout, no blocking, robots.txt clean. No bare '/collections/new-releases', '/new-arrivals', '/whats-new', '/just-in', '/new-in', or '/latest' page exists (all 404). Sitemap grep (156 collection handles) surfaced 5 category-scoped pages: /collections/new-releases-{seating,accent-chairs,storage,outdoor,dining}. Each has a real filterable product grid (facets: Configuration Type/Material/Color/Type, Sort By) and an on-page H3 heading naming the category (e.g. 'Seating'), and every one's <title> explicitly reads 'New Releases: {Category} Furniture Collection'. None of these 5 pages are linked from the main header nav or the homepage (checked full homepage collection-link dump, and the category pages themselves e.g. /collections/sofas-sectionals do not link to their new-releases counterpart) -- they read as a real but currently-unlinked (e.g. reachable via email/direct link) merchandising taxonomy, not editorial/marketing pages, so they are recorded as genuine New Arrivals PLPs per the 'real listing + genuinely represents new additions' test. No shared parent groups them (breadcrumbs are flat, e.g. Home>Seating / Home>Outdoor -- the breadcrumb does not say 'New Releases'), so they are emitted as 5 sibling rows, not a parent+children group. Also found /collections/fall-preview (breadcrumb Home>Fall Preview, title 'Fall Preview Furniture Collection', H3 'Fall Preview', 25 real products, also unlinked from nav) -- flagged ambiguous: 'preview' language plausibly maps to the brief's 'New This Season' target term, but every item on the page carries a live percentage-off discount badge and the page is not clearly distinguished from a seasonal sale curation (only 5/25 items overlap with Bestsellers, so it isn't simply a re-list of existing top items, but genuineness as 'recently added' vs 'seasonal marketing selection' could not be confirmed). Note: the whole site is currently running a sitewide 'Labor Day Sale' banner, so discount badges appear on New Releases pages too and are not by themselves a sale-page signal.
